Bassist Greig “Chubby” Jackson is one of the most dynamic performers in jazz history. He was born in New York in 1918 and started playing bass professionally in 1935. He was the spark plug behind the driving rhythm section in the first great Woody Herman band and brought Ralph Burns and Neil Hefti to the attention of Woody, who said of Chubby, “What an immense influence he had on us. And what enthusiasm!” He has performed and recorded with Charlie Barnet, Conte Candoli, Terry Gibbs, Gerry Mulligan and many others. Chubby was recognized as the major bassist of 1945 by Down Beat and was named a Gold Award winner by Esquire Magazine in 1947. His talents also were employed for a successful Chicago children’s television show and he has conducted clinics and workshops on jazz with his son, drummer Duffy Jackson.
Chubby lives in San Diego with his wife Margo, and he remains a treasure of jazz lore.
Chubby was interviewed in San Diego, California on February 14, 1998, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
